summary: [ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE — NOT A REAL DEFECT] Illustrative: APPROVED enrollment accepted for INACTIVE employee without validation
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Insert employee with employment_status=INACTIVE. 2. Insert APPROVED enrollment for that employee. 3. Query enrollments table.
expected_result: INSERT should be rejected OR application layer should flag the violation.
actual_result: INSERT succeeds without error (application-level rule not enforced at DB level for this scenario).
evidence_reference: This is an INTENTIONAL DESIGN NOTE, not a real defect. The schema enforces many rules via CHECK/FK constraints but BR-04 (eligibility and status check) requires an application-layer or trigger. See sql_validations.sql VQ-13/VQ-14 and test TC-E06.

summary: [ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE — NOT A REAL DEFECT] Illustrative: Duplicate APPROVED enrollment not blocked at DB constraint level
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Insert two APPROVED enrollments with the same employee_id and plan_id but different enrollment_id values. 2. Both INSERTs succeed.
actual_result: Both rows are accepted; violation only detectable by application-level SQL check VQ-09.
evidence_reference: This is an INTENTIONAL DESIGN NOTE. A UNIQUE constraint on (employee_id, plan_id, status) would enforce this at the DB level. Documented as a known limitation in README.md.
